text: Traditionally when teachers teach writing. <break time="0.8s" /> They assign topics for students to write on perhaps they do a bit of brainstorming about the topic. <break time="0.8s" /> During a pre writing phase. <break time="0.8s" /> And then have students write about the topic. <break time="0.8s" /> Without interruption. <break time="0.8s" /> Subsequently teachers collect and evaluate. <break time="0.8s" /> What students have written. <break time="0.8s" /> Such instruction is very product oriented. <break time="0.8s" /> There is no involvement of the teacher. <break time="0.8s" /> In the act or process of writing. <break time="0.8s" /> In process writing, on the other hand. <break time="0.8s" /> Students may initially brainstorm ideas about a topic. <break time="0.8s" /> And begin writing. <break time="0.8s" /> But then they have repeated conferences. <break time="0.8s" /> With the teacher and the other students. <break time="0.8s" /> During which they receive feedback. <break time="0.8s" /> On their writing up to that point. <break time="0.8s" /> Make revisions. <break time="0.8s" /> Based on the feedback they receive. <break time="0.8s" /> And carry on writing. <break time="0.8s" /> In this way. <break time="0.8s" /> Students learn to view their writing. <break time="0.8s" /> As someone elses reading. <break time="0.8s" /> And to improve both the expression of meaning. <break time="0.8s" /> And the form of their writing. <break time="0.8s" /> As they draft and redraft. <break time="0.8s" /> Process writing shifts the emphasis in teaching writing. <break time="0.8s" /> From evaluation to revision.
